The Crest & Crag Difference

A considered way to climb, explore and experience Tanzania.

From the first conversation to the final step on the mountain, every journey is shaped around thoughtful planning, local knowledge and a calm, personal approach. We do not believe in rushed itineraries or one-size-fits-all adventures — we believe in clear preparation, honest guidance and a journey designed around you.

01 — LOCAL KNOWLEDGE

Guided by people who know the mountain.

Our approach is grounded in local experience, clear communication and a team that understands the rhythm of Kilimanjaro and Tanzania — so your journey feels informed, authentic and confidently led.

02 — CARE & SAFETY

Prepared for the journey, not just the summit.

Good preparation matters. We focus on sensible pacing, practical guidance, altitude awareness and support throughout your journey, helping you arrive stronger, calmer and ready for the climb.

03 — PERSONAL PLANNING

Your itinerary should feel like yours.

03 / Choose Your Route

Find your
way up.

Every route tells a different story. Choose the path that matches your pace, your ambition and the experience you want to remember — from scenic trails through the rainforest to the quiet, demanding steps toward Uhuru Peak. With Crest & Crag, your climb is carefully planned around you, with experienced local guidance and thoughtful support from the trailhead to the summit.

01 · ROUTE
7–8DAYS

Lemosho

Lemosho is a scenic and beautifully gradual approach to Kilimanjaro, beginning in the lush rainforest before opening into wide alpine landscapes with unforgettable views of the mountain. With more time to acclimatize and a quieter trail experience, it is an ideal choice for climbers who want to take in the journey, build steadily toward the summit and reach Uhuru Peak with confidence.

View route ↗
02 · ROUTE
6–7DAYS

Machame

Machame is one of Kilimanjaro’s most rewarding routes, taking you from lush rainforest through dramatic alpine landscapes to the summit of Uhuru Peak. With gradual acclimatization, breathtaking scenery and a strong sense of adventure, it is a journey designed for those who want to experience the mountain step by step.

View route ↗
03 · ROUTE
8–9DAYS

Northern Circuit

Circle Kilimanjaro beyond the crowds. The Northern Circuit follows the mountain’s quieter northern slopes, opening wide views toward Kenya and giving you more time to acclimatize, breathe deeply and experience the mountain as a true wilderness journey.

View route ↗
04 / More Ways Up

Choose another
route.

Every mountain route has its own rhythm. Explore another way to experience Tanzania’s high country with Crest & Crag — from the classic Marangu trail to the northern wilderness of Rongai, the direct challenge of Umbwe, the volcanic drama of Mount Meru and a one-day Kilimanjaro experience.

01 · ROUTE
5–6DAYS

Marangu

5–6 DAYS5 NightsHuts

The classic “Coca-Cola” route, moving through rainforest, moorland and the alpine desert toward Kibo. A steady journey with hut accommodation and a beautiful acclimatization day at Horombo.

View route ↗
03 · ROUTE
5–6DAYS

Umbwe

5–6 DAYS5 NightsDirect Ascent

A steep, raw and direct approach from the southern flank. Umbwe moves quickly into high country before joining the Southern Circuit at Barranco — a route for strong, experienced trekkers.

View route ↗
02 · ROUTE
6–7DAYS

Rongai

6–7 DAYS6 NightsNorth Approach

Approach Kilimanjaro from the quiet northern side near the Kenyan border, then cross toward Mawenzi and Kibo before descending through the Marangu side of the mountain.

View route ↗
04 · MOUNTAIN
3–4DAYS

Mount Meru

3–4 DAYS3 Nights4,566 m

A dramatic climb inside Arusha National Park, combining wildlife-rich lower slopes, volcanic ridges and a sunrise summit on Socialist Peak — an exceptional mountain journey in its own right.

View route ↗
05 · DAY EXPERIENCE
1DAY

Kilimanjaro Day Trip

1 DAYMandara HutMarangu Gate

Step onto Kilimanjaro without committing to a summit expedition. Hike through the rainforest to Mandara Hut, with time for the Maundi Crater viewpoint before returning the same day.

View route ↗

Crest & Crag · Lemosho Route

Lemosho
8 Days.

A scenic western approach through rainforest, Shira Plateau and the dramatic southern circuit before the summit.

8 Days7 Nights
5,895 mUhuru Peak
WestApproach
Day 1Lemosho Gate → Forest Camp

Into the rainforest

Meet the mountain team, complete park formalities and begin the gradual walk through Kilimanjaro’s western rainforest.

Day 2Forest → Shira 1

Forest to open country

Leave the dense forest behind as the trail rises toward the Shira Plateau and wider mountain views.

Day 3Shira Plateau

Across the high plateau

Continue across the Shira landscape with a steady pace designed to support acclimatization.

Day 4Shira → Barranco

Into the southern circuit

Cross high alpine terrain toward Lava Tower and descend toward Barranco, building valuable acclimatization through altitude gain and loss.

Day 5Barranco → Karanga

Over the Barranco Wall

Climb the Barranco Wall with your guide, then continue across the alpine desert toward Karanga Camp.

Day 6Karanga → Barafu

Base camp for the summit

Make the final approach to Barafu Camp, rest and prepare carefully for the night summit attempt.

Day 7Summit → Mweka

Uhuru Peak

Begin before dawn for the summit. Reach Uhuru Peak, celebrate the achievement and descend toward Mweka Camp.

Day 8Mweka → Gate

Descent and farewell

Complete the descent through forest to the park gate, meet your transfer and return to Arusha or Moshi.

Your route. Your rhythm.

Crest & Crag · Route Preparation

Prepare with confidence.

A scenic western approach with rainforest, Shira Plateau and the southern circuit before the summit.

Challenging · gradual acclimatizationDifficulty
Mountain tentsAccommodation
3 fresh meals daily on the mountainMeals
Guide · cook · porters · health monitoringMountain Support

What to Bring

  • Layered warm clothing and a waterproof outer layer
  • Comfortable, broken-in trekking footwear and spare socks
  • Headlamp, water bottles or hydration system, sunglasses and sunscreen
  • Personal toiletries, medication and any required medical documents
  • Personal trekking gear can be arranged for rental in Arusha where available

Safety & Turn-Around

Your mountain team monitors your wellbeing throughout the expedition. Daily pacing, altitude management, weather and trail conditions are assessed by the guide team, and the itinerary may be adjusted or a turn-around recommended when safety or health requires it.

First briefing: you will receive the key safety, health, route and preparation guidance before the climb begins.

Baggage & Porter Guidance

Porter support is included where stated in your expedition inclusions. Keep your daypack focused on the essentials you personally need during hiking, while the team will explain packing and luggage arrangements during the pre-climb briefing.

Food & Dietary Needs

Meals are freshly prepared during the mountain expedition as described in the route inclusions. Please tell Crest & Crag about vegetarian, gluten-free or other dietary requirements before travel so your meal plan can be prepared appropriately.

Before You Start

International flights, visas, personal insurance, personal trekking equipment and other exclusions remain the traveller's responsibility unless specifically arranged with Crest & Crag. Any requested private or single arrangements should be confirmed before booking.

Tipping: tips are not included. You will be informed and guided through the tipping arrangements during your first briefing, so you understand how it works before the climb begins.
Climb Transparency

Inclusions & Exclusions.

Carefully planned expeditions with honest, upfront guidance and no surprise expenses on the mountain.

Included in Lemosho Expedition

What Crest & Crag Provides

  • All Kilimanjaro National Park entry, conservation, and camping fees (8 days)
  • TANAPA mountain rescue service fees
  • Professional, certified mountain guides and dedicated mountain crew
  • Mountain cook, porters, and ethical crew welfare standards
  • High-grade waterproof sleeping tents (twin sharing) and thick foam mattresses
  • Spacious dining mess tent equipped with camp furniture
  • Three hot, nutritious and freshly prepared meals daily while on the mountain
  • Clean, boiled, and purified drinking water
  • Emergency medical oxygen and twice-daily pulse-oximeter health monitoring
  • Private roundtrip transfers between your Arusha/Moshi hotel and trailhead gate
  • Official Kilimanjaro summit certificate upon completion
  • Government taxes and 18% Tanzanian VAT included
Not Included

Climber Responsibilities

  • International and domestic flight tickets
  • Tanzanian tourist visa fees
  • Hotel accommodation before and after the climb
  • Comprehensive high-altitude travel and medical evacuation insurance
  • Personal trekking gear; gear rental available in Arusha
  • Customary gratuities and tips for guides, porters and cook
  • Alcoholic drinks, soft beverages and bottled mineral drinks
  • Personal laundry, telephone calls and miscellaneous expenses
  • Credit card / online payment processing surcharges, if applicable

Crest & Crag · Machame Route

Machame
7 Days.

The classic “Whiskey Route” — a beautiful, demanding climb through changing landscapes and strong summit preparation.

7 Days6 Nights
5,895 mUhuru Peak
SouthApproach
Day 1Machame Gate → Camp

Rainforest beginning

Complete registration and begin the climb through lush rainforest toward the first mountain camp.

Day 2Machame → Shira

Into the moorland

Rise above the forest into open moorland and continue toward the Shira Plateau.

Day 3Shira → Barranco

Acclimatization day

Cross the high landscape toward Lava Tower before descending toward Barranco, using altitude gain and loss to support acclimatization.

Day 4Barranco → Karanga

Barranco Wall

Climb the Barranco Wall with steady guidance, then traverse the alpine desert toward Karanga.

Day 5Karanga → Barafu

Summit preparation

Reach Barafu Camp, settle in early and prepare your clothing, equipment and energy for summit night.

Day 6Barafu → Uhuru → Mweka

Summit day

Start before dawn, climb toward Stella Point and continue to Uhuru Peak. After the summit, descend toward Mweka Camp.

Day 7Mweka → Gate

Descent and farewell

Complete the descent through the forest to the park gate, meet your transfer and return to Arusha or Moshi.

Because Kilimanjaro is not simply a mountain you visit. It is a challenge you prepare for, a story you live, and a memory you carry home.

02

Discover Kilimanjaro through Lemosho, Machame, Northern Circuit, Rongai, Marangu, Umbwe, Mount Meru and our one-day mountain experience. Different routes, different rhythms — one unforgettable goal.

Move through rainforest, open moorland, alpine desert and the high slopes of Kibo. Every landscape reveals something new, and every step brings you closer to the Roof of Africa.

CREST & CRAG · SAFETY & MOUNTAIN INFORMATION

Safety & Mountain
Information.

Everything you should understand before stepping onto Kilimanjaro — from altitude and acclimatization to packing, hydration, weather and the support of your mountain crew.

DISCOVER THE JOURNEY ↗
01

Altitude & Acclimatization

Kilimanjaro rises quickly from the foothills to high altitude. A well-paced itinerary gives your body time to adapt. We encourage a steady pace, regular hydration, rest and attention to how you feel each day.

Acclimatization is one reason route and itinerary length matter. Longer itineraries can provide more time on the mountain and more opportunity to adapt gradually.

02

Mountain Safety

Safety starts with preparation and continues throughout the climb. Our guides monitor the group, the trail and changing conditions, while keeping communication clear so decisions can be made responsibly.

If a traveller becomes unwell or conditions become unsuitable, the priority is always sensible action rather than pushing toward a target at any cost.

03

What To Pack

Bring practical layers for changing temperatures, comfortable trekking footwear, rain protection, warm summit clothing, personal medication, sun protection and a reliable water bottle or hydration system.

Your exact packing list depends on the route, season and personal needs. Ask us for a tailored checklist before your climb.

04

Clothing & Equipment

Expect very different conditions as you climb: warm lower slopes, cooler forest and moorland, exposed alpine terrain and freezing summit conditions. Layering lets you adjust without carrying unnecessary bulk.

Crest & Crag can help you understand what to bring and what can be arranged locally, including rented mountain equipment where available.

05

Hydration & Nutrition

Regular drinking and consistent meals are important on the mountain. Small, frequent snacks can help you maintain energy during long trekking days.

Tell us about dietary preferences or requirements before arrival so the team can prepare appropriately.

06

Weather & Best Time

Kilimanjaro weather changes with altitude and season. Conditions can shift quickly, especially higher on the mountain. Your guide will help you respond to the conditions you actually encounter.

There is no single perfect day on the mountain; choosing a suitable season and route, preparing well and allowing enough time are all part of the planning.

07

Emergency & Medical Information

Before departure, tell us about relevant medical or dietary requirements and any medication you need to carry. During the climb, communicate symptoms early rather than waiting for them to become severe.

For any medical concern, follow professional medical advice and the instructions of your mountain guide. In an emergency, the guide team will coordinate the appropriate response available for the situation.

08

Guides, Porters & Mountain Support

A Kilimanjaro expedition is a team effort. Guides lead and support the journey, while cooks, porters and camp teams help make the expedition possible.

Respect, communication and responsible treatment of the mountain crew are part of the experience we want every traveller to have.

YOUR NEXT STEP

Ready to understand the mountain
before you climb it?

Tell us your route, dates and questions. We will help you prepare for the journey with clear information and a plan built around you.

Crest & Crag · About Us
03 / About Crest & Crag

Built for the
mountain. Made for
the journey.

Crest & Crag Tanzania Safaris is a Kilimanjaro-focused travel company built around a simple belief: reaching the summit is only one part of the adventure. The real journey lives in the preparation, the people, the changing landscapes, the rhythm of the trail and the feeling of discovering Tanzania from the inside.

03 / The mountain experience

A journey shaped by the mountain.

At Crest & Crag, we believe the mountain experience is about more than the summit. It is about preparation, perspective, resilience and the feeling of standing in a landscape that stays with you long after the trail.

Kilimanjaro Tanzania Mountain Experience
01 · Our beginning

A mountain company with a Tanzanian point of view.

Crest & Crag was created to offer a more considered way to experience Kilimanjaro. We believe a great expedition should feel personal from the first conversation — not like a standard package that simply moves a traveller from gate to gate.

Our work is rooted in Tanzania: its mountains, its people, its landscapes and the hospitality that makes northern Tanzania special. We combine local understanding with careful planning so travellers can arrive prepared, climb with confidence and experience the mountain with respect.

02 · The mountain

Kilimanjaro is not conquered in a hurry.

At 5,895 metres, Kilimanjaro moves through rainforest, heath, moorland, alpine desert and the high summit world in a single extraordinary journey. Every altitude brings a different landscape — and a different reason to slow down, listen to your body and trust the process.

For us, good guiding means understanding that rhythm. Route choice, pacing, acclimatization, hydration, rest, weather awareness and daily communication all matter. The summit is important, but the way you reach it matters too.

03 · What we believe

Prepare with purpose.
Climb with confidence.

04 · Our people

Guides are more than the people who lead the trail.

A mountain expedition is built by people. Our guides are there to read the trail, watch the conditions, keep communication clear and help travellers make sensible decisions throughout the climb.

Behind every successful expedition is also a wider team: cooks, porters, camp support and the local partners who make the journey possible. We believe their knowledge, dignity and contribution are part of the experience — not something hidden behind the itinerary.

05 · Safety & preparation

Confidence begins before the mountain.

Good preparation removes uncertainty. Before a climb, we help travellers understand their route, what to pack, how the days are structured, what conditions can feel like at altitude and what support is available along the way.

We approach safety as an everyday practice: thoughtful planning, appropriate pacing, communication, observation and respect for the mountain. The goal is not to rush toward a photograph at the summit, but to create a journey where the traveller feels informed and supported from start to finish.

06 · What we stand for

Local knowledge. Safety. People. Purpose.

Local knowledge. We believe a Kilimanjaro journey is stronger when it is shaped by people who understand the mountain, its seasons, its routes and the communities around it. Our approach is grounded in Tanzania and designed around the reality of the mountain rather than a generic travel template.

Safety and preparation. The strongest expeditions begin before the first step. We put careful route planning, acclimatization, clear communication, sensible pacing and responsible decision-making at the heart of the journey. We want guests to understand what the mountain asks of them and to feel supported throughout the climb.

The mountain crew matters. Guides, cooks and porters are not background details. They are central to the expedition. We believe their knowledge, contribution and dignity should be respected, and that the people who make the journey possible should be treated as part of the experience.

Thoughtful service. From the first conversation to the final day, we aim for personal attention, clear information and practical support. Dietary needs, preparation questions, route choices and logistics should have a human answer — not a one-size-fits-all response.

Responsible travel. Kilimanjaro is not simply a backdrop. It is a living landscape and part of Tanzania's natural and cultural heritage. We believe in travelling with respect for the mountain, local communities and the places that welcome us.

Mountain to safari. Kilimanjaro can be the beginning of a wider Tanzania journey. After the summit, the experience can continue through northern Tanzania's wildlife, landscapes and communities, connecting the mountain adventure with the country beyond it.

07 · Routes with character

There is no single way to experience Kilimanjaro.

Lemosho, Machame, Northern Circuit, Rongai, Marangu and Umbwe each carry a different personality. Some favour longer acclimatization, some offer a more direct mountain experience, and some approach Kilimanjaro from a quieter side. We help travellers choose with the whole journey in mind — time, fitness, expectations, scenery and the experience they want to remember.

Beyond Kilimanjaro, Mount Meru and our Tanzania safari journeys allow the mountain story to continue into the wider landscapes and wildlife of northern Tanzania.

08 · Beyond the summit

Climb Kilimanjaro. Then see more of Tanzania.

The mountain can be the beginning rather than the end. After the trail, Tanzania opens into a different kind of wilderness — savannah, wildlife, open skies, local communities and the unforgettable landscapes of the northern safari circuit.

That is why Crest & Crag is built around both mountain and safari experiences. We want travellers to experience Tanzania as a whole, not simply pass through it on the way to a summit.

09 · Our standard

Thoughtful planning. Clear communication. Genuine care.

From the first WhatsApp message to the final day in Tanzania, we aim to make every stage clear. We listen to what you want, explain what the journey requires and build the details around your trip rather than asking you to fit into a rigid template.

We are here for travellers who want more than a tick on a bucket list: people who want to understand the mountain, meet the people behind the journey and leave Tanzania with a deeper connection to the place.

10 · The Crest & Crag promise

We do not simply take you up the mountain.

We prepare you for the journey, guide you through the experience and stay close to the details that matter. Our purpose is simple: to create Kilimanjaro and Tanzania journeys that feel well considered, deeply local and worth remembering long after the trail disappears behind you.

01 · Start the conversation
A thoughtful first step

Tell us what
you have in mind.

Good trip planning starts with the right questions. Kilimanjaro operators commonly make space for route choice, group size, dates, contact details, preparation, safety questions and special dietary needs. We have brought those practical details into one clear form so you do not have to explain your journey twice.

Whether you need help choosing between Lemosho, Machame, Northern Circuit or another route, want to ask about equipment, or need to tell us about a gluten-free, vegetarian, vegan, halal or other dietary requirement, put it here.

DIETARY REQUIREMENTS / FOOD NOTES

When you submit, the information above will be prepared into one WhatsApp message and opened in WhatsApp for you to send to Crest & Crag.

02 · Frequently asked questions
Which Kilimanjaro route should I choose?

There is no single route that fits everyone. We look at your time, hiking background, preferred scenery, acclimatization needs and the kind of mountain experience you want before suggesting a route.

Do I need previous climbing experience?

Kilimanjaro is a trekking expedition rather than a technical climbing ascent, but altitude and long trekking days still require preparation. We can help you understand the physical demands before you book.

How do you handle special dietary requirements?

Tell us in advance about gluten-free, vegetarian, vegan, halal, allergies or other dietary requirements. The earlier we know, the better we can plan meals and logistics around your needs.

Can I combine Kilimanjaro with a Tanzania safari?

Yes. We can help connect your mountain journey with northern Tanzania safari experiences so the climb becomes part of a wider trip rather than a separate booking.

What if I have questions before booking?

That is exactly what this page is for. Send your details through the form and your full enquiry will open in WhatsApp so our team can continue the conversation with the context already included.

Do you provide or rent climbing equipment?

Tell us what you already have and what you still need. We can discuss the equipment requirements and rental arrangements available for your trip.

What happens if weather or mountain conditions change the plan?

Mountain itineraries can be affected by weather, park rules and safety conditions. The guiding team may adjust pacing or the itinerary when necessary, with safety and the wellbeing of travellers as the priority.

Terms of Service.

01

Acceptance of Terms

02

Bookings, Deposits & Payments

• A 30% deposit is required to confirm your booking.

  • Bookings are confirmed only after the required deposit has been received.
  • Payments must be made through our approved payment methods.

03

Cancellation & Refund Policy

  • Cancellation must be made in writing.
  • Refunds depend on the cancellation date and costs already committed to suppliers.
  • Certain park fees, permits, accommodation and third-party charges may be non-refundable.
  • Late cancellation, failure to travel or no-show may result in non-refundable costs already committed to suppliers.
  • We recommend travel insurance to protect your trip investment.
04

Itinerary, Changes & Safety Decisions

We carefully plan every trip, but itineraries may change due to weather, park regulations, safety conditions or other circumstances beyond our control.

For mountain climbs, our guides may adjust, shorten, stop or change the itinerary when necessary to protect the safety and wellbeing of guests.

For Kilimanjaro and Mount Meru, the guide or relevant park authority may decide that a guest should not continue to a higher altitude, reach the summit or proceed with a planned activity when safety requires a different decision. A summit is therefore not guaranteed.

05

Travel Insurance & Health

  • Travel insurance is strongly recommended for all travelers.
  • For Kilimanjaro and Mount Meru climbs, guests should be physically prepared and disclose any relevant medical or fitness concerns before the trek.
  • Guests should promptly inform the guide or trip team of any illness, injury, altitude-related symptoms or other condition that may affect safe participation.
06

Passport, Visa & Travel Documents

Guests are responsible for ensuring that their passport, visa and other required travel documents are valid and available for travel.

07

Client Responsibilities & Conduct

  • Guests must provide accurate information needed for booking, transport, accommodation and trip planning.
  • Guests must follow reasonable instructions from guides, drivers, accommodation providers and relevant park or tourism authorities.
  • Guests are expected to respect local communities, staff, other travelers, wildlife, park rules and the natural environment.
  • Unsafe, abusive, threatening or seriously disruptive conduct may result in a guest being removed from an activity or trip where necessary for safety or the wellbeing of others.
08

Equipment & Rental Responsibility

Where tents, camping equipment, hiking equipment or other items are rented or supplied for a trip, the equipment remains subject to the applicable owner or supplier conditions.

  • Guests should use rented or supplied equipment responsibly and return it in reasonable condition.
  • Loss or damage caused by misuse, negligence or failure to follow reasonable care instructions may result in a charge for repair or replacement, where applicable.
09

Accommodation, Transport & Third-Party Suppliers

Accommodation, airport transfers, vehicles, guides, permits and other services may involve third-party suppliers and are subject to availability and supplier conditions.

Where a reasonable substitution is necessary, Crest & Crag may arrange an alternative of a comparable standard where practical. Supplier-specific conditions may also apply.

Trip-specific details such as the final itinerary, inclusions and exclusions, accommodation, transport arrangements, permit requirements, payment deadlines and any agreed changes should be confirmed in writing as part of the booking.

Guests should review the final booking confirmation and ask us about any point they do not understand before travel.

11

Personal Belongings

Guests are responsible for the safe care of their passports, money, electronics, luggage and other personal belongings throughout the trip. Where storage or handling is provided by a third party, that provider's conditions may apply.

Complaints & Trip Issues

If an issue arises during a trip, guests should raise it with our team as soon as reasonably possible so that we have an opportunity to investigate and, where possible, resolve it during the trip.

Formal complaints should be submitted in writing using the contact details below.

DATA PROTECTION · TRANSPARENCY

Privacy Policy.

How Crest & Crag Tanzania Safaris safely, responsibly and transparently handles your personal information.

EFFECTIVE DATE: 7 SEPTEMBER 2026
01

Introduction

Welcome to Crest & Crag Tanzania Safaris. We are committed to protecting your privacy and ensuring that your personal information is handled safely, responsibly, and transparently.

This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, store, and protect your personal information when you visit our website, contact us, request a quotation or book a safari, Kilimanjaro climb, or other travel services with us.

We process personal information in accordance with applicable laws and regulations of Tanzania, including the Personal Data Protection Act, 2022 and applicable regulations.

02

Information We Collect

Depending on the services you request, we may collect the following information:

Personal Information

  • Full name
  • Email address
  • Telephone or WhatsApp number
  • Nationality
  • Passport or identification details when required for bookings or permits
  • Billing and payment information, including relevant transaction or payment-status details where needed to confirm your booking.

Travel Information

  • Safari or Kilimanjaro booking details
  • Travel dates
  • Accommodation preferences
  • Dietary requirements
  • Emergency contact information
  • Special requests related to your trip

Website Information

When you use our website, we may automatically collect:

  • IP address
  • Browser type
  • Device and operating system
  • Pages visited
  • Website usage information
  • Cookies and similar technologies where applicable
03

How We Use Your Information

We use your information to:

  • Respond to your enquiries and requests.
  • Prepare quotations and travel itineraries.
  • Process and confirm safari and mountain-climbing bookings.
  • Arrange accommodation, transportation, park permits and other travel services.
  • Communicate with you about your trip.
  • Process payments and issue invoices or receipts.
  • Provide customer support.
  • Improve our website, services and customer experience.
  • Comply with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

We only collect and use information that is reasonably necessary for these purposes.

04

Sharing Your Information

Crest & Crag Tanzania Safaris does not sell or rent your personal information to third parties.

We may share relevant information only when reasonably necessary to provide the services you request, including with:

  • Accommodation and hospitality partners.
  • Mountain guides, crew and service providers involved in your trip.
  • Transport providers and other operational partners.
  • Government authorities, park authorities or permit offices where required.
  • Payment providers and financial institutions where necessary to process your payment.

Where information is shared, we take reasonable steps to ensure it is handled appropriately and only for the relevant purpose.

Payment & Communication Providers

Depending on the payment or communication method you choose, relevant information may be processed by third-party providers such as payment processors, banks, mobile-money services, WhatsApp or other communication platforms. Those providers may process information under their own privacy policies and terms.

05

Data Security

We take reasonable measures to protect your personal information from unauthorised access, loss, misuse, alteration or disclosure.

  • Access to personal information is limited to people who need it for legitimate business or service purposes.
  • We use reasonable administrative and technical safeguards to protect information.
  • We take appropriate steps when information is transmitted or shared with service providers.
  • We continuously review our practices to improve the protection of your information.

While we take reasonable precautions, no online system or method of transmission can be guaranteed to be completely secure.

06

Why We Process Your Information

We process personal information where it is necessary to respond to your request, perform or prepare for a booking, comply with applicable legal obligations, protect legitimate business interests, or where you have provided consent where consent is required.

The specific basis may depend on the information involved and the service you request.

07

International Transfers & Service Providers

Some service providers or platforms used to operate communications, payments, hosting, analytics or travel services may process information outside Tanzania. Where this occurs, we take reasonable steps to use appropriate providers and safeguards consistent with applicable requirements.

08

Data Incidents

If we become aware of a personal-data incident affecting information we control, we will assess it and take reasonable steps required by applicable law, including appropriate notification where legally required.

09

How Long We Keep Your Information

We retain personal information only for as long as reasonably necessary to provide our services, maintain business records, meet legal or regulatory obligations, resolve disputes, and enforce our agreements.

When information is no longer required, we take reasonable steps to securely delete, anonymise or otherwise dispose of it.

10

Your Rights

Depending on applicable law, you may have rights regarding your personal information, including the right to:

  • Request access to the personal information we hold about you.
  • Request correction of inaccurate or incomplete information.
  • Request deletion of information where legally applicable.
  • Withdraw consent where processing is based on consent.
  • Raise a concern about how your personal information is handled.
  • Request information about how your personal information is used.

We may need to verify your identity before responding to certain requests.

11

Cookies

Our website may use cookies and similar technologies to improve website functionality, understand how visitors use our website, remember preferences, and support a better browsing experience.

You may be able to control or disable cookies through your browser settings. Some website features may not function correctly if certain cookies are disabled.

12

Third-Party Websites

Our website may contain links to third-party websites, platforms or services. These third parties may have their own privacy policies and practices.

Crest & Crag Tanzania Safaris is not responsible for the privacy practices, content or security of third-party websites. We encourage you to review the privacy policy of any external service before providing personal information.

Third-Party Services

Third-party services used to support bookings, payments, communications, hosting or analytics may process information independently of Crest & Crag Tanzania Safaris. Their handling of information is governed by their own privacy notices and terms.

13

Children’s Privacy

Our services are intended for travellers and customers who can lawfully provide personal information. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children without appropriate consent where such consent is required by law.

If you believe a child has provided personal information to us without appropriate consent, please contact us so that we can review and take appropriate action.

14

Your Privacy Matters

Your privacy matters to us. We are committed to respecting your privacy and protecting your personal information while helping you plan and experience Tanzania responsibly.

15

Changes to This Privacy Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time to reflect changes in our services, legal requirements, technology or privacy practices.

When changes are made, we will update the effective date shown at the beginning of this policy. We encourage you to review this page periodically so you remain informed about how we protect your personal information.

16

Contact Us

Crest & Crag · Mountain Journal

Beyond
the Summit

More than the moment you reach Uhuru Peak. This is the mountain life between the trail, the camp, the food, the people and the quiet stories that stay with you long after the descent.

01 / THE EXPERIENCE

Feel the mountain.
Live the journey.

We shaped Beyond the Summit as a visual journal of the experience our guests actually remember: sunrise above the clouds, a warm cup at camp, a good mountain meal after a long day, and a guide who knows when to push and when to slow the pace.

The structure takes inspiration from leading expedition brands that make the people, food, preparation and mountain atmosphere part of the story — not just the summit photograph.

02 / MOUNTAIN LIFE

Morning Above the Clouds

Quiet trails, thin air and that first light touching the slopes of Kilimanjaro.

Mountain Food

After the Trail

07 / THE GUIDE

A guide, not a title.

Your mountain guide is part navigator, part teacher, part storyteller and part safety lead. At Crest & Crag, the guide experience is central to the climb.

We focus this page on the person leading you through the mountain — not porter profiles — because the guest-facing story should begin with the guide who walks with you.

Route KnowledgeReading terrain · weather · pace
Mountain SafetyAltitude awareness · daily checks
Local StoryTanzania · culture · mountain life
Summit RhythmCalm pace · patience · focus

Come for the summit.
Remember the journey.

From the first briefing in Tanzania to the final descent, Crest & Crag is here to make the mountain feel personal, considered and unforgettable.

02 / Mountain Life

Morning Above the Clouds

Before the mountain fully wakes, Kilimanjaro offers a quieter kind of magic — cold air, open sky and the first light resting on the slopes.

When the clouds fall below you.

There is a moment on the mountain when the trail seems to rise above the ordinary. The clouds settle below, the horizon opens and the changing light makes every step feel worth taking.

At Crest & Crag, we believe the mountain is not only about reaching a point on the map. It is about noticing these quiet moments — the thin air, the silence, the changing colours and the feeling of being completely present.

Mountain LifeQuiet trails · Thin air · First light · Kilimanjaro
The Crest & Crag WayThoughtful pacing, local knowledge and a journey designed around the experience — not just the summit.

Want to experience this morning?

Ask Crest & Crag about the routes, seasons and itinerary that can put you above the clouds at the right moment.

04 / The Team

The people who carry the mountain with you.

Behind every summit story is a team whose strength, experience and care make the journey possible. On Kilimanjaro, porters are not background to the climb — they are an essential part of it.

More than what they carry.

A porter carries far more than a pack. They help move the practical heart of a mountain expedition — tents, food, cooking equipment, water and camp essentials — so trekkers can focus on the trail and the experience ahead.

But their importance goes beyond the weight on their shoulders. Their knowledge of the terrain, camp rhythm and changing mountain conditions becomes part of the quiet support that surrounds each day on Kilimanjaro.

At Crest & Crag, we believe a great climb should also be a respectful journey. The people who help make your summit possible deserve recognition, dignity and appreciation every step of the way.

The Crest & Crag WayRespect the people behind the journey. Walk together, communicate clearly and remember that every summit is a team achievement.
StrengthReliable support through long days, steep trails and changing altitude.
ExperienceLocal mountain knowledge that helps the team move with confidence and awareness.
TeamworkYour climb is shared work — from the first camp to the final descent.
RespectThe journey matters more when the people who make it possible are valued.

Meet the people behind your climb.

Want to know more about how Crest & Crag builds its mountain team and prepares your Kilimanjaro journey?

06 / Summit Day

The longest morning.
The moment you came for.

Before sunrise, Kilimanjaro asks for patience. The air is cold, the trail is quiet and every step is deliberate. Then the horizon begins to change — and the mountain gives you a morning you will remember for years.

Before the sun, there is the climb.

Summit morning begins in darkness. Headlamps trace a narrow line through the night while your guide keeps the pace calm, steady and purposeful.

There is no rush to prove anything. The goal is to move well, listen to your body and let the mountain reveal itself one step at a time.

As the sky begins to brighten, the cold gives way to colour. First light reaches the surrounding peaks, the clouds fall away below you and the meaning of the journey becomes clear.

The Crest & Crag WayPatient pacing, experienced guiding, altitude awareness and thoughtful support — so summit day feels challenging, safe and deeply personal.
Early StartWe begin before sunrise to give the climb the time and rhythm it deserves.
Steady PaceSlow, deliberate movement helps conserve energy and keeps the experience controlled.
Mountain AwarenessYour guide watches conditions, altitude response, weather and the group throughout the ascent.
First LightFrom darkness to golden horizon, the changing light becomes part of the summit story.
Reach the roof of Africa

Make summit morning a memory.

Tell us about your Kilimanjaro plans and we will help you choose a route, pace and itinerary designed around the experience you want.

05 / Camp Life

After the trail, the mountain becomes home.

When the day's walking is done, camp becomes more than a place to sleep. It is where tired legs recover, warm food restores the body and the stories of the day begin to settle in.

The quiet side of the climb.

There is a different rhythm at camp. Boots come off. Layers are changed. A hot drink reaches your hands and the mountain suddenly feels still.

At Crest & Crag, we see camp life as part of the expedition itself — not a pause between important moments. It is where you recover, reconnect and prepare for the next morning with a clear mind.

From the first evening on the trail to the night before your summit push, these small routines create some of the memories that stay with you long after Kilimanjaro is behind you.

The Crest & Crag WayGood mountain days need good recovery. Thoughtful pacing, warm meals, organised camp and genuine care make the journey feel complete.
RestA calm camp gives your body the space it needs after a long day at altitude.
WarmthSimple comforts, hot drinks and nourishing food matter when the air turns cold.
ConnectionCamp is where guides, guests and the mountain team share stories and reset together.
PreparationEvery evening is also preparation for the trail, the weather and the next day's goal.

Ready to experience camp life on Kilimanjaro?

03 / The Table

Mountain Food

Warm, nourishing meals designed around the reality of high-altitude trekking — breakfast, trail lunch, dinner, hot drinks and energy for summit day.

Good food is part of the climb.

Mountain meals should be more than a checkbox. The focus is warm, practical food that gives you energy without making the high-altitude day feel heavier.

Dietary needs can be discussed before departure, including vegetarian and gluten-free preferences.

BreakfastPorridge, eggs, toast, pancakes, fruit and hot drinks.
Trail LunchPractical packed or camp lunch with carbohydrates, protein, fruit and a warm option where possible.
DinnerSoup, rice or pasta, vegetables, stew and a simple dessert or fruit.
Mountain DrinksTea, coffee, hot chocolate and hydration support around camp.
Special DietsVegetarian and gluten-free options available when arranged in advance.

Food is part of the journey.

Tell us about your dietary preferences before departure and we will prepare the mountain experience around you.

Classic Kilimanjaro · The Coca-Cola Route

The Marangu Route

A classic journey through Kilimanjaro’s rainforest, heath and alpine desert, with the comfort of mountain huts and a dedicated acclimatization day at Horombo before the summit push.

6 Days5 Nights
5,895 mUhuru Peak
HutsAccommodation
Day 11,860 m → 2,720 m

Marangu Gate to Mandara Huts

After registration at Marangu Gate, enter the lush montane rainforest and climb steadily toward Mandara Huts. The first day is a gentle introduction to the mountain with rich vegetation and forest views.

◉ HIKING TIME: 3–4 HOURS
Day 22,720 m → 3,720 m

Mandara Huts to Horombo Huts

Leave the rainforest behind and move through open heath and moorland toward Horombo. Kibo and Mawenzi begin to dominate the horizon as the landscape opens.

◉ HIKING TIME: 5–7 HOURS
Day 33,720 m

Horombo Acclimatization Day

Take a dedicated acclimatization day around Horombo with a guided walk toward Zebra Rocks or the Mawenzi area, allowing your body to adjust while you enjoy the mountain scenery.

◉ HIKING TIME: 3–5 HOURS OPTIONAL WALK
Day 43,720 m → 4,703 m

Horombo Huts to Kibo Huts

Cross the alpine desert of the Saddle between Mawenzi and Kibo. The trail becomes quieter and more exposed as you approach Kibo for an early meal, final checks and rest before summit night.

◉ HIKING TIME: 5–6 HOURS
Day 54,703 m → 5,895 m → 3,720 m

Summit Push: Kibo Huts to Uhuru Peak, Down to Horombo

Begin around midnight and climb through the darkness toward the crater rim. Reach Uhuru Peak at 5,895m, celebrate the Roof of Africa, then descend to Horombo for recovery and rest.

◉ HIKING TIME: 12–15 HOURS TOTAL
Day 63,720 m → 1,860 m

Horombo Huts to Marangu Gate

Descend through the moorland and rainforest to Marangu Gate. Collect your summit certificate, say goodbye to the mountain crew and transfer back to your hotel.

◉ HIKING TIME: 5–7 HOURS
The Marangu Experience

Why choose Marangu?

  • Mountain-hut accommodation instead of tent camping.
  • A classic route with a clear, well-established trail through changing ecological zones.
  • A dedicated acclimatization day at Horombo for a more measured summit approach.
  • A memorable summit route followed by a descent through the same beautiful mountain corridor.

Prepare with confidence.

The classic hut route through rainforest, heath and alpine desert with a dedicated acclimatization day.

Baggage & Porter Guidance

Porter support is included where stated in your expedition inclusions. Keep your daypack focused on the essentials you personally need during hiking, while the team will explain packing and luggage arrangements during the pre-climb briefing.

Food & Dietary Needs

Meals are freshly prepared during the mountain expedition as described in the route inclusions. Please tell Crest & Crag about vegetarian, gluten-free or other dietary requirements before travel so your meal plan can be prepared appropriately.

Before You Start

International flights, visas, personal insurance, personal trekking equipment and other exclusions remain the traveller's responsibility unless specifically arranged with Crest & Crag. Any requested private or single arrangements should be confirmed before booking.

Tipping: tips are not included. You will be informed and guided through the tipping arrangements during your first briefing, so you understand how it works before the climb begins.

OUR STORY & PASSION

More than a hike.
A feeling you carry home.

We are born and raised in the mountain shadows of northern Tanzania. From the high volcanic crags of Kilimanjaro to the wildlife plains of the Serengeti, our journey began on the trail.

For us, Kilimanjaro is not simply a destination to tick off a list. It is a place of perspective, connection and unforgettable moments — where every step reveals something new about the mountain, Tanzania and yourself.

“Embrace the Crest, conquer the Crag.”

Northern Approach · Near the Kenyan Border

The Rongai Route

A quieter northern approach to Kilimanjaro, beginning near the Kenyan border and crossing open moorland toward Mawenzi and Kibo before descending through the Marangu side.

7 Days6 Nights
5,895 mUhuru Peak
NorthApproach
Day 11,950 m → 2,620 m

Nalemoru Gate to Simba Camp

Drive to the northern trailhead, complete registration and begin through the forest toward Simba Camp. The quieter northern approach gives the expedition a calm beginning.

◉ HIKING TIME: 3–4 HOURS
Day 22,620 m → 3,450 m

Simba Camp to Second Cave

Continue upward through heath and moorland toward Second Cave, with broad northern views and a steady gain in elevation.

◉ HIKING TIME: 3–4 HOURS
Day 33,450 m → 3,600 m

Second Cave to Kikelewa Camp

Move across open moorland toward the dramatic Mawenzi massif. The landscape becomes increasingly alpine as you settle into Kikelewa Camp.

◉ HIKING TIME: 3–4 HOURS
Day 43,600 m → 4,300 m

Kikelewa Camp to Mawenzi Tarn Hut

Climb toward Mawenzi Tarn, one of the most dramatic camps on Kilimanjaro. The afternoon can be used for gentle exploration and acclimatization around the tarn.

◉ HIKING TIME: 3–4 HOURS
Day 54,300 m → 4,700 m

Mawenzi Tarn Hut to Kibo Hut

Cross the Saddle toward Kibo Hut through the stark alpine desert. Rest, hydrate and prepare carefully for the summit night ahead.

◉ HIKING TIME: 5–6 HOURS
Day 64,700 m → 5,895 m → 3,720 m

Summit Push: Kibo Hut to Uhuru Peak, Down to Horombo

Begin the summit push in the early hours, climb toward the crater rim and reach Uhuru Peak at 5,895m. After celebrating, descend to Horombo Hut for rest.

◉ HIKING TIME: 12–14 HOURS TOTAL
Day 73,720 m → 1,860 m

Horombo Hut to Marangu Gate

Descend through moorland and rainforest to Marangu Gate, collect your summit certificate and transfer back to your hotel in Moshi or Arusha.

◉ HIKING TIME: 4–6 HOURS
The Rongai Experience

Why choose Rongai?

  • A northern approach with a quieter feel and wide views toward Kenya and the surrounding plains.
  • A gradual route that builds through forest, moorland and the alpine desert.
  • Beautiful Mawenzi scenery and a memorable overnight at Mawenzi Tarn.
  • Summit from Kibo followed by a descent on the Marangu side for a varied mountain experience.

Direct Southern Ascent · High Challenge

The Umbwe Route

A steep and direct southern approach that quickly leaves the rainforest behind before joining the Southern Circuit at Barranco. This itinerary is suited to strong trekkers prepared for demanding terrain and rapid early elevation gain.

6 Days5 Nights
5,895 mUhuru Peak
DirectAscent Style
Day 11,600 m → 2,940 m

Umbwe Gate to Umbwe Camp

Enter the rainforest and climb the narrow, steep Umbwe ridge. The trail rises quickly through dense vegetation before reaching Umbwe Camp above the forest.

◉ HIKING TIME: 5–7 HOURS
Day 22,940 m → 3,950 m

Umbwe Camp to Barranco Camp

Continue through heath and moorland toward Barranco, where the trail joins the Southern Circuit. Dramatic cliffs and the Barranco Valley announce the change in landscape.

◉ HIKING TIME: 4–5 HOURS
Day 33,950 m → 4,033 m

Barranco Camp to Karanga Camp

Tackle the famous Barranco Wall before crossing a series of ridges and valleys toward Karanga. A shorter day helps you conserve energy for the upper mountain.

◉ HIKING TIME: 4–5 HOURS
Day 44,033 m → 4,550 m

Karanga Camp to Barafu Camp

Climb through the alpine desert toward Barafu Base Camp. After arriving, complete a final health and gear check, eat early and rest for the summit attempt.

◉ HIKING TIME: 4–5 HOURS
Day 54,550 m → 5,895 m → 3,100 m

Summit Push: Barafu to Uhuru Peak, Down to Mweka Camp

Start around midnight and climb the upper slopes toward Stella Point and Uhuru Peak. After the summit, descend through the southern slope to Mweka Camp for a well-earned recovery night.

◉ HIKING TIME: 11–14 HOURS TOTAL
Day 63,100 m → 1,640 m

Mweka Camp to Mweka Gate

Make the final descent through lush rainforest to Mweka Gate. Receive your summit certificate, celebrate with the crew and transfer back to your hotel.

◉ HIKING TIME: 3–4 HOURS
The Umbwe Experience

Why choose Umbwe?

  • A direct and steep route with a strong sense of adventure from the first day.
  • Low traffic and a rawer mountain atmosphere before joining the Southern Circuit.
  • Rapid access to high terrain for trekkers with strong fitness and mountain experience.
  • A dramatic summit approach through Barafu and the southern descent through Mweka.

Arusha National Park · Socialist Peak

Mount Meru

A four-day volcanic mountain expedition through wildlife-rich forest, giant heather and an exposed summit ridge, ending at Socialist Peak with wide views across northern Tanzania and toward Kilimanjaro.

4 Days3 Nights
4,566 mSocialist Peak
HutsAccommodation
Day 11,500 m → 2,514 m

Momella Gate to Miriakamba Hut

Meet the ranger and begin across open grassland before entering montane forest. Wildlife-rich lower slopes, giant fig trees and forest scenery lead toward Miriakamba Hut.

◉ HIKING TIME: 4–5 HOURS
Day 22,514 m → 3,570 m

Miriakamba Hut to Saddle Hut

Climb through changing vegetation into the giant-heather and moorland zones. Reach Saddle Hut, then take an optional acclimatization walk toward Little Meru before returning to camp.

◉ HIKING TIME: 4–6 HOURS INCLUDING OPTIONAL WALK
Day 33,570 m → 4,566 m → 2,514 m

Summit: Saddle Hut to Socialist Peak, Down to Miriakamba

Begin before dawn along the crater rim toward Rhino Point and Socialist Peak. Watch sunrise from the summit, then descend to Saddle and continue to Miriakamba for the night.

◉ HIKING TIME: 10–12 HOURS TOTAL
Day 42,514 m → 1,500 m

Miriakamba Hut to Momella Gate

Make the final descent through forest and open slopes toward Momella Gate. Meet the vehicle and transfer back to Arusha after completing the Mount Meru expedition.

◉ HIKING TIME: 3–4 HOURS
The Mount Meru Experience

Why choose Mount Meru?

  • A complete mountain adventure with wildlife-rich lower slopes inside Arusha National Park.
  • A dramatic volcanic crater rim and sunrise summit at Socialist Peak.
  • Mountain-hut accommodation and an armed ranger escort in the wildlife zone.
  • An exceptional standalone climb and a natural high-altitude preparation option for a later Kilimanjaro expedition.

One Day · Marangu Gate to Mandara Hut

Kilimanjaro Day Trip

A one-day introduction to Kilimanjaro through the rainforest to Mandara Hut, with an optional Maundi Crater viewpoint before returning to the gate the same day. This is a lower-mountain hike, not a summit attempt.

1 DayDay Experience
2,720 mMandara Hut
~12 kmRound Trip
OUR STORY & PASSION

More than a hike.
A feeling you carry home.

We are born and raised in the mountain shadows of northern Tanzania. From the high volcanic crags of Kilimanjaro to the wildlife plains of the Serengeti, our journey began on the trail.

For us, Kilimanjaro is not simply a destination to tick off a list. It is a place of perspective, connection and unforgettable moments — where every step reveals something new about the mountain, Tanzania and yourself.

“Embrace the Crest, conquer the Crag.”

Day 11,860 m → 2,720 m → 1,860 m

Marangu Gate to Mandara Hut & Back

Depart early from Arusha or Moshi and drive to Marangu Gate for registration. Hike through the lush montane rainforest to Mandara Hut, enjoy lunch and, when conditions allow, walk to the Maundi Crater viewpoint before descending the same trail to the gate and returning to your hotel.

◉ HIKING TIME: 5–7 HOURS TOTAL
The Day Trip Experience

Why choose the Kilimanjaro Day Trip?

  • Experience the rainforest zone of Kilimanjaro without committing to a multi-day expedition.
  • Reach Mandara Hut and, when appropriate, the Maundi Crater viewpoint for panoramic northern Tanzania views.
  • A practical option for travellers with limited time or for a gentle mountain introduction.
  • Return to Arusha or Moshi the same day after a guided hike with a local mountain team.

Grand 360° Traverse · Northern Slopes

The Northern Circuit

Kilimanjaro’s newest and longest expedition. Circle the mountain through remote northern slopes, gradual altitude acclimatization and wide-open wilderness — a journey designed to experience Kilimanjaro from a deeper, quieter perspective.

9 Days8 Nights
~98 kmTrek Distance
5,895 mUhuru Peak
HighestSuccess Rate
WildernessCamping Style
360°Mountain Traverse
Day 12,100 m → 2,650 m

Londorossi Gate to Mti Mkubwa (Big Tree Camp)

Following hotel pickup in Arusha or Moshi, drive to Londorossi Gate on Kilimanjaro’s western flank for registration formalities. Begin your introductory trek through dense moss-covered rainforest, with possibilities of seeing black-and-white colobus monkeys in the canopy before settling into Mti Mkubwa Camp for dinner and rest.

◉ HIKING TIME: 3–4 HOURS
Day 22,650 m → 3,610 m

Mti Mkubwa to Shira 1 Camp

Climb out of the rainforest canopy into the expansive volcanic Shira Plateau. The landscape changes quickly from forest to open heath and moorland, revealing your first clear views of Kibo Peak across the open plain.

◉ HIKING TIME: 5–6 HOURS
Day 33,610 m → 3,850 m

Shira 1 Camp to Shira 2 Camp

A gentle, unhurried traverse across the volcanic plateau toward Shira 2 Camp. The steady elevation gain helps your body adjust naturally to altitude while the open terrain creates panoramic views toward Mount Meru rising above the western clouds.

◉ HIKING TIME: 3–4 HOURS
Day 43,850 m → 4,200 m

Shira 2 Camp to Moir Hut

Leave the Shira Plateau behind and continue north toward Moir Hut, a remote high-altitude camp away from the busier southern trail. The day introduces a wilder side of Kilimanjaro, with rugged volcanic terrain and a quiet sense of space.

◉ HIKING TIME: 5–7 HOURS
Day 54,200 m → 4,020 m

Moir Hut to Buffalo Camp

Climb out of the Moir Valley and continue eastward around the northern slopes. The trail rises and falls through dramatic, increasingly sparse landscapes, with expansive views across the northern wilderness and toward the Kenyan plains.

◉ HIKING TIME: 5–6 HOURS
Day 64,020 m → 3,870 m

Buffalo Camp to Third Cave

Traverse quiet valleys and rolling alpine desert ridges around the northern slopes of Kibo. The scenery becomes increasingly remote as you move eastward, ending the day at Third Cave Camp in a peaceful high-mountain setting.

◉ HIKING TIME: 4–5 HOURS
Day 73,870 m → 4,790 m

Third Cave to School Hut

Ascend steadily through the alpine desert toward the saddle between Kibo and Mawenzi peaks, arriving at School Hut by early afternoon. Complete health checks, hydrate, eat early and prepare your equipment before resting for the demanding summit night ahead.

◉ HIKING TIME: 4–5 HOURS
Day 84,790 m → 5,895 m → 3,100 m

Summit Push: School Hut to Uhuru Peak, Down to Millennium Camp

Begin the midnight push toward Uhuru Peak through the darkness, following the steep upper slopes toward the crater rim. Reach Uhuru Peak at 5,895m, celebrate the Roof of Africa, then descend on the southern side toward Millennium Camp for much-needed rest after the longest day on the mountain.

◉ HIKING TIME: 11–14 HOURS TOTAL
Day 93,100 m → 1,640 m

Millennium Camp to Mweka Gate

A celebratory final descent through lush rainforest back to Mweka Gate. Receive your official Kilimanjaro summit certificate, celebrate with your mountain crew and transfer back to your hotel in Moshi or Arusha carrying the memory of a complete circuit around Africa’s highest mountain.

◉ HIKING TIME: 3–5 HOURS
The Northern Circuit Experience

Why choose Northern Circuit?

  • The longest Kilimanjaro route, giving you more time to acclimatize and settle into the mountain.
  • A remote traverse around the quieter northern slopes with fewer crowds and expansive wilderness views.
  • A true 360° mountain experience, showing Kilimanjaro from western, northern and eastern perspectives.
  • A gradual, thoughtfully paced journey guided by Crest & Crag with careful preparation, safety and support.
